newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP merger "deal of century" in France - Bebear.
newsitem.headline: UAP merger "deal of century" in France - Bebear.

text.p: Axa chairman Claude Bebear said on Tuesday that his company's merger with UAP was the "deal of the century in French insurance" and would create a player that did away with a weak French reputation in the financial sector.

The groups are merging to create what they said would be the world's second largest insurer and biggest in asset management, with a turnover of over 300 billion francs ($59.3 billion), more than 100,000 staff and a stock market capitalisation of 100 billion francs.
"It's the deal of the century for French insurance. We're both delighted," Bebear told reporters after a news conference on the merger.

"This marriage of two French companies is crucial because we have given France a truly exceptional financial player. We have shown that even if we are sometimes seen as weak in France we can be the best," he said.

"There is a striking geographical complementarity on the one hand and also at every level where we do business. I have never seen an alliance -- and we've been involved in a few -- which creates so much synergy."
"I have always been convinced that in order survive in the 21st century you absolutely have to have a world-scale business and a size which allows you to compete with the big boys," said Bebear.
"Individually we were already among the big boys and now we are the big boy."

Bebear said in the news conference: "In with a globalising insurance business marked by mega-mergers you have to choose -- either you look for a niche and specialise or you become a big global player. We chose the second path."
Bebear said all major shareholders including BNP were aware of and backed the planned merger which involves an exchange of four Axa shares for 10 UAP shares.
Each four-for-10 exchange will also carry four certificates of contingent value which guarantee a price for UAP shares of 157 francs, slightly above the price at which UAP was privatised in 1994.
The privatisation price for small investors was 152 francs and it was a little higher for institutional shareholders and core shareholder groups such as BNP.
A statement from the companies showed that assets managed by the two groups totalled 2,295 billion francs at June 30, 1996 -- 1,552 billion for Axa and 743 billion for Union des Assurances de Paris.
The geographical logic for the merger boils down mainly to merging Axa's prowess in North America and Asia with UAP's European prominence.

At the world level, the merged group has combined turnover based on 1995 annual figures of 313.1 billion francs -- 155.3 billion in the case of Axa and 157.8 billion in the case of UAP, a statement showed

In Europe, where the merged group will be the largest in insurance, combined turnover based on 1995 figures is 97.7 billion francs, compared to individual turnover figures of 20.4 billion francs for Axa and 77.3 billion for UAP.

At operational level, the two firms said sources of savings included increased capacity and a more rationalised structure in the mass risks insurance business, lower asset management costs, rationalisation of planned investment in life insurance in Germany as well as a wider product range and more powerful network in cross-border life insurance.
